newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Grinacon to expand overseas.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Grinacon to expand overseas.

text.p: South Africa's Grinaker Construction Ltd, which is to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange next month, will launch an offshore expansion drive over the next three years to underpin earnings growth.

Grinacon managing director Bean Bornheimer said late on Thursday the company, which was recently unbundled from Grinaker Holdings Ltd, aimed to expand international operations to 20 percent of turnover by 2000 from eight percent now.
He said opportunities were being investigated in southern and central Africa as well as Southeast Asia.

"We are looking at southern and central Africa as a growth market. A lot of these countries are getting support from the World Bank and civil engineering opportunities are opening up," Bornheimer said at an investment analysts meeting.
He said Grinacon had recently landed two contracts in Malaysia to build concrete sleepers. "We are thinking of investing seven to 10 million rand there to produce sleepers."

In a bid to widen its margins from 2.8 percent in the 1995/96 financial year to an expected 4.5 percent within three years, Grinacon would also focus on growing its building products division to opencast mining operations.

Bornheimer said he was not very optimistic about the outlook for South Africa's building industry in 1997 as hotel construction was currently at its peak. However, some construction could be sparked by the expected award of gambling licences from March next year.
He said a huge boon for the industry would be if Cape Town was awarded the 2004 Olympic Games, where construction work would be worth an estimated seven billion rand.

Grinacon, which will be listed on the JSE's building and construction sector on December 2, was unbundled from its parent to enable it to trade at prices closer to the underlying value of its business, Bornheimer said.

In the year to June 30, Grinacon achieved profit before tax of 41 million rand on turnover of 1.9 billion rand. Earnings per share rose to 81.2 cents from 85.6 the previous year, with the dividend up to 18 cents from 15.
